content:
Apple has been notably slow to launch a folding iPhone, and one of the reasons that has been cited is the company's dissatisfaction with the visible creases and durability problems of early-generation flexible screens.

Screen partner Samsung has finally solved the problems to Apple's satisfaction. The Korean company's latest foldable phone gives us a preview of what the iPhone Ultra screen will look like…

The long-awaited folding iPhone

Apple will launch its own iPhone version a full six years after the first folding Android phone hit the market. The first Samsung Galaxy Fold's screen was extremely prone to damage, with Samsung even having to pull it from sale in an emergency – and the wisdom of this wait was immediately confirmed.

From this, it appears Apple has been waiting for flexible screen technology to mature to the point where no crease is visible once the device is unfolded. Reports indicate Apple had to send in its own design engineers to help Samsung meet this target.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8

While the version of the screen ultimately used in the iPhone Ultra will not necessarily be identical to the just-launched Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, the two should be extremely similar.

This panel is actually not making its debut here. Samsung briefly showed a prototype of the screen back in January, then quickly removed it from public view. It seems someone inside the company quickly realised this technology needed to be kept under wraps – not least, one imagines, because it will be used in an Apple product.

Andrew Romero from sister site 9to5Google was impressed by this new screen.

He also noted that the crease on the previous generation became more pronounced with repeated opening and closing, but based on his brief hands-on time with the new device, that problem appears to be a thing of the past.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to be unveiled in September alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, featuring a 5.3-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen.
